# Sūrah al-Baqarah (Chapter 2) — Expanded Verse-by-Verse Commentary

## Introduction to the Sūrah

**Expanded Commentary**

**The Longest Chapter and Its Place in the Book**

Sūrah al-Baqarah, named for the cow in verses 67-73, is the longest chapter with 286 verses, revealed in Madinah after Hijrah, and forms a constitution for the first Muslim polity. It treats theology, sacred history, law, worship, social and economic order, and ethics. The chapter follows al-Fātiḥah, whose petition “Guide us along the Straight Path,” (1:6) is answered by “This is the Book! There is no doubt about it—a guide for those mindful ˹of Allah˺,” (2:2). Its opening pages delineate three human groups that structure the sūrah's argument.

**Madinan Legislation and Theological Depth**

Unlike Makkan sūrahs focused on creed and afterlife, al-Baqarah addresses a community that owns property, concludes contracts, raises families, and defends its city. It legislates prayer direction, fasting, pilgrimage, alms, marriage, divorce, nursing, orphans, usury, trade, loans, war, and capital justice. It contains the Throne Verse and the final two verses, both singled out in authentic reports. Muslim records: “Recite Sūrat al-Baqarah, for holding to it is blessing and abandoning it is sorrow, and the deceivers have no power over it.” (Muslim 804) and “Do not turn your houses into graves; indeed, Satan flees from a house in which Sūrat al-Baqarah is recited.” (Muslim 780) and “Whoever recites the two verses from the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah in a night, they will suffice him.” (Bukhari 5009; Muslim 808).

The scribe should not refuse to write as Allah has taught them to write. They will write what the debtor dictates, bearing Allah in mind and not defrauding the debt. If the debtor is incompetent, weak, or unable to dictate, let their guardian dictate for them with justice. Call upon two of your men to witness. If two men cannot be found, then one man and two women of your choice will witness—so if one of the women forgets the other may remind her. The witnesses must not refuse when they are summoned. You must not be against writing ˹contracts˺ for a fixed period—whether the sum is small or great. This is more just ˹for you˺ in the sight of Allah, and more convenient to establish evidence and remove doubts. However, if you conduct an immediate transaction among yourselves, then there is no need for you to record it, but call upon witnesses when a deal is finalized. Let no harm come to the scribe or witnesses. If you do, then you have gravely exceeded ˹your limits˺. Be mindful of Allah, for Allah ˹is the One Who˺ teaches you.
